name: אֱלִישָׁמָע
gloss: my God has heard; God has heard
summary: Borne by the leader of Ephraim in the wilderness, Elishama son of Ammihud, who brought Ephraim’s offering on the seventh day and led its host when Israel set out from Sinai (Num 1:10; 7:48; 10:22), grandfather of Joshua (1Ch 7:26–27); by a son of David born in Jerusalem (2Sa 5:16; 1Ch 3:8), with a brother called Elishama in 1Ch 3:6 where 2Sa 5:15 has Elishua; by the scribe in whose room Baruch’s scroll was laid (Jer 36:12, 20–21); by the grandfather of Ishmael who killed Gedaliah (2Ki 25:25; Jer 41:1); by a priest Jehoshaphat sent to teach the law (2Ch 17:8); and by a man of Judah (1Ch 2:41). It is אֵל “God” with the ־ִי of “my”, and שָׁמַע “he has heard”: the confession “God has heard” that Leah and Rachel made in naming Simeon and Dan (Gen 29:33; 30:6), and that Hagar was given in Ishmael’s name (Gen 16:11).

evidence.note: Over the host of the camp of the sons of Ephraim, אֱלִישָׁמָע בֶּן־עַמִּיהוּד.
For Ephraim, Elishama son of Ammihud, among the men who stood with Moses and Aaron to number Israel.
On the seventh day, the leader of the sons of Ephraim, Elishama son of Ammihud, brings his offering.
Ammihud his son, Elishama his son, Nun his son, Joshua his son.
Among the sons born to David in Jerusalem.
Elishama the scribe, in whose chamber the princes sat.
Ishmael son of Nethaniah son of Elishama, of the royal seed.
Elishama and Jehoram the priests, sent to teach in Judah.
“God heard (וַיִּשְׁמַע אֱלֹהִים) the voice of the boy”: אֱלֹהִים and שָׁמַע together, as in the name.
“This poor man cried, and Yahweh heard (שָׁמֵעַ).”

note: BDB files the name under אֵל (a.dl.bg, root אלה); it is linked here to the shama entry for its verb, as eliab is linked to av for its noun. Phoenician names of the type šmʿ-DN and DN-šmʿ (ŠMʿBʿL, BʿLŠMʿ) are formed the same way (see the phn-shm cognate). The ־ִי may be the suffix “my” or a joining vowel. TIPNR’s Elishua@2Sa.5.15 is named Elishama in 1Ch 3:6; the bdb key limits the name entry to this spelling. Num 1:10 and 1Ch 7:26 make the Ephraimite leader Joshua’s grandfather; TIPNR keys him Elishama@Num.1.10.
